title: The J.D. Marshall, 1911: the shipwreck off Indiana Dunes State Park

beats.text: There's a shipwreck about 30 feet down, off the beach at Indiana Dunes State Park.
beats.label: INDIANA DUNES STATE PARK
beats.credit: Indiana DNR; Indiana University Underwater Science

beats.text: She's the steamer Marshall, a wooden ship built in 1891 to haul lumber. Around 1910, she was rebuilt to pump sand from the lake bottom.
beats.label: BUILT 1891
beats.credit: Indiana DNR; Indiana University Underwater Science

beats.text: That June, anchored off the dunes near Chesterton, she sprang a leak. The crew patched it.
beats.label: JUNE 1911
beats.credit: Indiana DNR marker; Indiana University Underwater Science

beats.text: Then, early on June 11, 1911, a squall blew in from the west. The patch failed, and the ship rolled over.
beats.label: JUNE 11, 1911
beats.credit: Indiana DNR marker; Michigan City Evening Dispatch (1911)

beats.text: Four of her crew were lost.
beats.label: FOUR LOST
beats.credit: Indiana DNR; Indiana University Underwater Science

beats.text: Decades later, salvagers raised the wreck and tried to haul it away. It ended up back on the bottom.
beats.label: THE SALVAGE
beats.credit: Indiana University Underwater Science; Indiana Natural Resources Commission

beats.text: Her propeller now sits beside the park's beach pavilion. And in 2013, the wreck became Indiana's first underwater nature preserve.
beats.label: A PRESERVE SINCE 2013
